analysis.investment_thesis: Chalet Hotels trades at 28x earnings and 5x book — both grossly in excess of any margin of safety a prudent investor should demand. The earnings record is riddled with losses (five loss years in ten), making any calculation of 'proven earning power' impossible.
key_strengths: Operating cash flow strongly positive 5/5 recent years, reaching INR 950 Cr in FY2025
Revenue CAGR of 12.8% over nine years shows real demand for its properties
Promoter holding at 67.33% aligns management with the business long-term
key_risks: P/B of 4.99x means investors pay nearly five times net asset value — a catastrophic price if occupancy deteriorates
Capex surged to INR 969 Cr in FY2025, flipping free cash flow negative (-14 Cr) despite strong operations
Debt/Equity of 0.73 breaches my 0.5 ceiling; borrowings were INR 2,489 Cr in FY2025
red_flags: Five loss years out of ten (2016, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022) — no consistent earning power established
P/E of 28.2x and P/B of 4.99x: both far exceed Graham's absolute limits of 15x and 1.5x respectively
FY2025 net profit collapsed to INR 142 Cr from INR 278 Cr in FY2024 despite revenue growth — margin compression is real
analysis.detailed_analysis:
By every quantitative measure I require, Chalet Hotels fails. The Graham Number — the ceiling price derived from earnings and book value — is rendered meaningless by an erratic profit history; the average 'earned' profit over a decade is negligible after netting out the loss years. At P/B of 4.99x, the market prices in a durable premium that the volatile income statement does not justify. Hospitality is inherently cyclical, as COVID demonstrated brutally: operating income fell from INR 337 Cr in FY2020 to just INR 7 Cr in FY2021.

The massive capital expenditure programme (INR 969 Cr in FY2025 alone, rising CWIP to INR 122 Cr) signals management is expanding aggressively — precisely the opposite of the financial conservatism I prize. Free cash flow turned negative in FY2025. Financing cash inflows of INR 496 Cr suggest the company is funding growth partly through fresh capital. Until the balance sheet strengthens materially, the price falls well below 1.5x book, and five or more consecutive years of profits are established, I would not place a single rupee here.
